campaigns.notes: Correctness: the segmented run (97 cooperative launches / chunk) produces a BYTE-IDENTICAL token stream to uniseg (1 launch) — same first token 874, same PLOW_IDS, argmax device==host AGREE. On the SAME object the segments run identical math, so Stage 1 is EXPECTED to be neutral+tax; the +0.43% is the K-1 extra launch+sync tax. The occupancy WIN requires the Stage-2 occ-2 lean object, which is blocked on per-segment re-slicing (the emitter slices for n_cu=188; occ-2 fills 2*188=376 resident blocks). Host enqueue tax measured at 3.08 us/launch (299 us / 97 launches) — negligible vs the ~514 ms GEMM-bound compute.

Unflagged emission byte-identical (cmp verified vs pre-change binary on a ctx-8192 pkt).
campaigns.occ2_unblocked: T9c's occ-2 premise assumed a ~40 KiB GEMM arena; the REAL arena is 60 KiB (PGM_STAGES=3 plain / GLU_STAGES=2, 128x128 tile). 2x60=120 KiB > the 100 KiB dynamic-smem cap => ptxas caps occupancy at 1 (SMEM-bound, NOT register-bound — 128 regs already passes). occ-2 reached only by shrinking the lean object's pipeline depth to 2/1 stages => arena 40 KiB => 2x=80 KiB < 100 KiB => runtime grid 376 (occ-2 x 188 SMs).

accounting_4k_isolation.note: Decomposition: plain segmentation tax +0.3% (T9c); re-slicing to 2*n_cu blocks on the SAME good full-arena object adds +8.7% (557.85 vs 514.92 — 2x GQ cursor atomics + 2x counter bumps + 2x gate polls, each block runs 2 slices at grid188); switching to the lean occ-2 object adds a FURTHER +33.5% (744.92 vs 557.85 — the 2/1 pipeline halving + 248 B spill). occ-2's second resident block does NOT recover the halved pipeline depth: the GEMM at occ-1/3-stage is already latency-hidden.

campaigns.verdict: NEGATIVE. occ-2 segmentation does NOT beat or approach vLLM prefill — it REGRESSES plow's own prefill by +22% (128k) to +45% (4k). The re-slicing tax (+9%) plus the arena/pipeline tradeoff (occ-2 is SMEM-bound, reachable only by halving the GEMM pipeline depth, which costs ~33%) together swamp the occupancy headroom. The gap SHRINKS with ctx (+45%/+40%/+22% at 4k/32k/128k) because the fixed re-slice overhead amortizes over the O(n^2)-growing GEMM compute — hinting the occ-2 thesis could approach break-even at very long ctx IF the pipeline-depth penalty were removed. That fair test needs an occ-2 object at FULL pipeline depth, reachable only by a smaller GEMM N-tile (BN 128->64, arena ~45 KiB) — a kernel-tiling change not attempted here. As implemented (stage-reduction, the low-risk lever), occ-2 is a clear loss.
